newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban take northeastern Afghan town.
newsitem.headline: Taleban take northeastern Afghan town.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia captured the strategic northeastern opposition-held town of Pul-i-Khumri in Baghlan province, witnesses said.
The town, on the main highway from the capital Kabul to northern Afghanistan via the Salang Pass, was first taken by new Taleban recruits from Baghlan. A Taleban convoy rolled into the town later.

Pul-i-Khumri was held by forces of Syed Jafar Naderi, allied to the main opposition alliance, whose leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum was forced to flee northern Afghanistan after a mutiny by his own ethnic Uzbek forces last week.

The Taleban convoy, about one km (half a mile) long, arrived via the strategic 11,000-foot (3,350-metre) high Salang Pass, which it crossed on Tuesday after being halted by opposition shelling for two days.

The Taleban advance cuts the last link between Hezb-i-Wahdat, a mainly Shi'ite faction still fighting the Taleban in the central province of Bamiyan, and Ahmed Shah Masood, military commander of the government driven from Kabul last September.
